AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 2, 2021
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDER N-15-21, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE
FROM A REMOTE LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING: YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO:
publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING
THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709
573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER
CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a)
  – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles County Sheriff representative, and other related City
  officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE § 54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Numbers 8056-015-014, 8056-015-016, and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; Michael F G Trust; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Roy Halberg
  Grace Brethren Church of Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Jodi Santos, Student Council President
  St. Linus Catholic School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize Hometown Heroes.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Presentation by Assembly Member Lisa Calderon.

  3.  Liberty Utilities Rate Increase presentation.

  4.  State of the City recap.
   5.  Relay for Life recap.

  6.  Halloween event recap.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES - Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of October
  19 and October 26, 2021. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period September 19, 2021 –
  October 2, 2021, in the total amount of $931,313.26. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  October 14 - October 27, 2021, in the total amount of $3,615,472.29. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by William Ekhtiar
  and Jesus Torres. 830-05/20

  Report

  6.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – OCTOBER 27, 2021 - No action is required unless the City
  Council elects to review the decision of the Planning Commission on those items where the
  Commission’s action was final. 320

  Report

  7.  RESOLUTION NO. 21-66 – APROVING REVISIONS TO THE CITY OF NORWALK FRAUD POLICY
  AND PROTOCOL - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-66, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING REVISIONS TO THE CITY OF
  NORWALK FRAUD POLICY AND PROTOCOL. 140-02

  Report

  8.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  9.  AMENDMENT NO. 10 TO THE AGREEMENT FOR STREET SWEEPING SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 10 to the agreement with Nationwide
  Environmental Services, a division of Joe’s Sweeping Inc.; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  this amendment, on behalf of the City; in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1045-07

  Report
 APPOINTMENTS

  10. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

PUBLIC HEARINGS

  11. ORDINANCE NO. 21-1729 - GRANTING A NON-PUBLIC UTILITY PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO
  HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED - Staff recommends City Council introduce by
  title only Ordinance No. 21-1729, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK GRANTING A
  PIPELINE FRANCHISE TO HERAEUS METAL PROCESSING, INCORPORATED, and schedule for a
  second reading. 618-16

  Report

  12. 2021-2029 DRAFT HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE - Staff recommends City Council receive public
  testimony, instruct staff to make any changes or corrections to the Draft Housing Element, and forward
  the Draft Housing Element to the Department of Housing and Community Development for review. 320-
  02-03

  Report

REPORTS

  13. RESOLUTION NO. 21-67 – BUDGET AMENDMENT - ENHANCEMENTS TO THE PUBLIC SAFETY
  DEPARTMENT - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-67, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL
  YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED BUDGET TO REDUCE FUNDS FOR ENHANCEMENTS TO PUBLIC
  SAFETY, in the amount of $206,726. 730-03-01

  Report

  14. SOCIAL SERVICE AGENCY FUNDING PROCESS AND COMMUNITY FUND ALLOCATION
  CHANGES TO ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT
  AND HOME INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 - Staff
  recommends City Council establish priorities for the social service agency application process and
  Community Fund allocations and provide direction for other on-going CDBG and HOME priorities for
  the FY 2022/23 Annual Action Plan. 425-03

  Report

  15. CITYWIDE PARKING STUDY RECOMMENDATIONS – Staff recommends City Council review and
  discuss the information provided and schedule for adoption at a future City Council meeting. 1050-02

  Report

  16. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – NOVEMBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 28, 2021.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
